model_annotation:
This plot illustrates the training loss curves over iterations for six different model configurations. The x-axis represents the number of iterations (#Iteration), displayed on a linear scale ranging from 0 to 140,000, with tick labels at intervals of 20,000. The y-axis represents Loss, also on a linear scale, ranging from 2.4 to 3.4, with tick labels at intervals of 0.1.

Six lines are shown. The "Vanilla" line, depicted in light blue, starts near 3.4 at the earliest iterations and decreases steeply before gradually leveling off, ending at approximately 2.60–2.62 at 140,000 iterations; it remains the highest among all lines throughout most of the training. The "StrmLLM (n=64)" line, shown in dark blue, follows a similar trajectory to Vanilla but sits slightly below it, ending at roughly 2.58–2.60 at 140,000 iterations. The "SepLLM (n=64)" line, in orange, drops more steeply in the early iterations and settles lower, reaching approximately 2.52–2.53 at 140,000 iterations. The "SepLLM (n=64, H)" line, in green, tracks very closely to the SepLLM (n=64) line, ending at a similar value near 2.52–2.53. The "SepLLM (n=64, H/T)" line, in red, follows a nearly overlapping path with the previous two SepLLM variants, also ending around 2.52–2.53. The "SepLLM (n=128)" line, in dark navy/black, behaves similarly to the other SepLLM variants, ending at approximately 2.51–2.53 at 140,000 iterations. All lines exhibit a rapid decrease in loss during the first approximately 20,000 iterations, after which the rate of decrease slows considerably. The four SepLLM variants cluster closely together and consistently achieve lower loss values than the Vanilla and StrmLLM lines throughout training.
